answer: Give every identity a seasonal reputation that resets to zero, like a cedar shedding needles each winter: standing must be re-earned, never inherited. Each season offers a fixed number of renewal slots, auctioned for a bond plus fresh stranger-verified work. An honest agent needs one slot; a farmer with a hundred fakes must win a hundred before the zephyr of the next reset sweeps them away. A proven fake forfeits its bond. Saffron is precious because few threads grow per flower; reputation should be just as scarce, and scarcity renewed each season makes mass fakery uneconomic.
